fdm.title: FDM 3D Printing
fdm.subtitle: Source high-performing parts for rapid prototyping and low-volume industrial production with FDM 3D printing. We offer an FDM printing service for quick-turn manufacturing using a variety of robust materials for many use cases and can print parts in 1 day.

blocks.x: FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling), also known as Fused Filament Fabrication, is an additive manufacturing process that heats thermoplastic filament and deposits it layer by layer to build parts from a digital CAD model. It is the most widely used 3D printing technology globally, accounting for the largest installed base of 3D printers worldwide. FDM is the first process engineers consider for rapid prototyping and functional parts due to its cost-effectiveness and versatility.

FDM builds parts by depositing melted filament onto a build platform layer by layer until the part is complete. The process starts with a digital design file translated into machine instructions. The filament is fed into a heated nozzle, melted, and extruded in thin strands along a programmed toolpath. Each strand cools and fuses to the previous layer to form a solid geometry. The build platform lowers after each layer, and the cycle repeats until the full part is produced.

items: Digital design file is converted to machine instructions
Thermoplastic filament is fed into the heated nozzle
Material melts and is extruded in thin strands
Nozzle moves along programmed toolpath (X, Y, Z axes)
Layers cool and fuse to form solid geometry
Build platform lowers for each new layer
Process repeats until part is complete

blocks.x: Materials Available in Our FDM Printing Service

We offer a wide range of thermoplastic materials for FDM printing, from commodity polymers to high-performance engineering plastics. Each material has unique properties suited for different applications.

items: PLA - Easy to print, excellent visual quality, ideal for concept models
ABS - Good strength and temperature resistance, suitable for functional parts
PETG - Food-safe, good strength, easy to print with balanced properties
Nylon (PA) - High strength, excellent wear and chemical resistance
TPU - Very flexible, ideal for flexible prototypes and seals

blocks.x: FDM is a cost-effective additive process that supports a wide range of thermoplastic materials. It offers fast turnaround for prototypes and low-volume production, straightforward material tradeoffs for strength and flexibility, and predictable scaling from desktop to industrial systems.

blocks.x: While FDM offers many advantages, it has some limitations compared to other 3D printing technologies. Understanding these drawbacks helps determine when FDM is the right choice for your project.

items: Visible layer lines may require post-processing for smooth finish
Lower resolution compared to SLA or SLS technologies
Anisotropic strength - parts are weaker across layer lines
Support structures required for overhangs, can be difficult to remove
Warping can occur with certain materials (especially ABS)
Not ideal for parts requiring very fine details or high cosmetic quality

blocks.x: Comparing FDM to Other 3D Printing Processes
FDM is one of several 3D printing technologies, each with unique strengths. Understanding the differences helps you choose the right process for your application.

items: FDM: Uses thermoplastic filament, strong functional parts, visible layers
SLA: Uses liquid resin, extremely high detail, smooth surface finish
FDM: Lower cost per part, wider material selection
SLA: Higher resolution, better for cosmetic and detailed prototypes
FDM: Requires support structures, extrudes melted filament
SLS: No supports needed, fuses powder with laser
FDM: Lower cost, faster for simple parts
SLS: More complex geometries possible, isotropic strength
FDM: Layer-by-layer extrusion, suitable for prototyping
MJF: Powder bed fusion, excellent for production parts
FDM: Lower machine cost, good for small quantities
MJF: Higher throughput, better mechanical properties
Rapid prototyping and design iteration
Functional parts requiring strength and durability
Low-volume production of 10-1000 parts
Applications where cost is a primary concern
Parts that don't require extremely fine detail or smooth surfaces
Projects needing quick turnaround (1-3 days)

injection-molding.title: Injection Molding
injection-molding.subtitle: Mass production of high-precision plastic parts in Chennai

blocks.x: Injection Molding is a manufacturing process used to produce plastic parts in large quantities by injecting molten plastic material into a custom-made metal mold. After cooling and solidifying, the part is ejected from the mold. VCAN 3D provides high-precision injection molding services in Chennai for automotive, industrial, and consumer applications.

items: Plastic granules are fed into a heated barrel
Material melts and becomes molten plastic
Molten plastic is injected into a metal mold under high pressure
Plastic cools and solidifies inside the mold
Finished part is ejected from the mold
Ideal for mass production
High precision & repeatability
Strong & durable parts
Smooth surface finish
Low cost per part (for high volumes)

blocks.x: SLA (Stereolithography) is a resin-based 3D printing technology that uses a UV laser to cure (harden) liquid photopolymer resin layer by layer to create highly detailed parts. VCAN 3D's SLA services in Chennai deliver exceptional accuracy and surface quality for prototypes and precision components.

items: Liquid resin is filled in a tank
UV laser scans the design layer by layer
Resin hardens where the laser hits
Platform moves layer by layer
Final part is cleaned & UV cured
Very high accuracy
Smooth surface finish
Great for detailed prototypes
Ideal for small & precision parts

sls-mjf-dlp.title: SLS / MJF / DLP 3D Printing
sls-mjf-dlp.subtitle: Advanced Industrial 3D Printing Technologies in Chennai

blocks.x: SLS (Selective Laser Sintering) is a 3D printing technology that uses a high-power laser to fuse powdered material (usually Nylon/PA12) layer by layer to create strong and functional parts. Unlike FDM, SLS does not require support structures because the surrounding powder supports the part during printing.

items: A thin layer of powder is spread on the build platform
Laser selectively fuses the powder as per CAD design
Platform lowers and new powder layer is spread
Process repeats layer by layer
Excess powder is removed after printing
No support structures required
Strong & durable parts
Complex geometries possible
Good for batch production

vacuum-casting.title: Vacuum Casting
vacuum-casting.subtitle: High-quality plastic parts in small batches using silicone molds

blocks.x: Vacuum Casting is a manufacturing process used to produce high-quality plastic parts in small batches using a silicone mold under vacuum conditions. VCAN 3D's vacuum casting service in Chennai is mainly used for low-volume production and for creating parts that closely resemble injection-molded components at a fraction of the cost.

items: A master model is created (usually by SLA/DLP 3D printing)
Silicone rubber is poured around the master to create a mold
Mold is placed inside a vacuum chamber
Liquid polyurethane resin is poured into the mold
Resin cures and the finished part is removed
Ideal for low-volume production (10–100+ parts)
Smooth surface finish
Multiple material options (ABS-like, rubber-like, transparent)
Lower cost compared to injection molding
Faster lead time
